memory_update.text: SPSC is the cleanest public pure-play for the retail EDI and trading-partner compliance network node; prioritize filing verification of recurring revenue, trading-partner count, retailer concentration, retention, and macro/tariff-related spending delays.
DSGX and OTEX are broader network-infrastructure candidates with B2B/EDI scale but require segment-purity checks before they can be ranked as direct consumer-retail chokepoint beneficiaries.
MANH belongs in the adjacent platform lane: not pure EDI, but important for retailer-specific order management, inventory visibility, store fulfillment, and omnichannel execution switching costs.

Need a follow-up Layer 1C/2 search for private competitors and M&A history around TrueCommerce, Orderful, Boomi, IBM Sterling, SAP, Oracle, Blue Yonder, and retailer-mandated EDI compliance portals to test whether public companies have durable bottleneck control.

node: Retail EDI and trading-partner compliance networks
summary: Layer 1B expands the public-company universe around retail EDI, trading-partner compliance, B2B connectivity, and adjacent omnichannel supply-chain execution platforms. The most direct pure-play candidate is SPS Commerce, whose disclosed retail-network positioning matches the node closely. Descartes and OpenText provide broader B2B/logistics/business-network infrastructure with EDI exposure but less pure retail dependence. Manhattan Associates is included as an adjacent platform leader in retail order-management and fulfillment orchestration rather than a pure EDI network. This is a research universe only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
